item.title: Neurons & genes: a CRISPR map of the mouse brain
item.dc:creator: A. Researcher
item.description:
Researchers used CRISPR screens to tag every neuron in a developing mouse cortex — and found that gene regulation, not cell lineage, predicts where a cell ends up.

The work took six years.

item.title: A very long dispatch about prime numbers
item.description: The Riemann hypothesis concerns the zeros of the zeta function, and every serious attempt to prove it has failed for more than a century. This dispatch walks through the history of the problem, the analytic tools that were invented along the way, the numerical evidence gathered by computers, the connection to the distribution of prime numbers, the Hilbert-Polya idea that the zeros are eigenvalues of some unknown operator, the random matrix statistics that Montgomery and Dyson noticed over tea, the function field analogue that Weil proved, and the reasons mathematicians still believe the conjecture is true despite the absence of any proof whatsoever, before ending with a short reading list.
